newsitem.title: USA: Montana's winter wheat crop 10 percent harvested.
newsitem.headline: Montana's winter wheat crop 10 percent harvested.

text.p: Montana's winter wheat crop was 10 percent harvested as of Sunday, ahead of the five-year average of two percent, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service reported.
The crop ratings declined from the previous week. Winter wheat was rated two percent very poor, six percent poor, 30 percent fair 54 percent good and eight percent excellent.
"Wheat stem saw fly infestation in parts of the state has prompted quite a bit of swathing of winter wheat," the report said. "Grain harvest is getting into full swing in those areas."
Spring wheat was ripe on one percent of the acreage, in line with average. The crop was rated one percent excellent, 12 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 40 percent good and seven percent excellent.
Barley was rated one percent very poor, five percent poor, 35 percent fair, 43 percent good and 16 percent excellent.
Pasture and range were rated two percent very poor, seven percent poor, 28 percent fair, 54 percent good and nine percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated seven percent very short, 33 percent short, 57 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
